architectural_implications.after: Define a flat per-step JSON record schema consumed by both debugging and automated tuning before agent behavior is finalized.
architectural_implications.before: Build agent, then add logging/dashboards when something breaks.
architectural_implications.consequence: The trace schema becomes a versioned interface; changing agent steps requires changing the record contract, and tuning pipelines break if it drifts.
architectural_implications.observation: Observability is a prerequisite layer that the tuning loop depends on, rather than a downstream add-on.

architectural_implications.after: A diagnoser agent analyzes drift, rewrites configurations, and triggers auto-tuning pipelines without human-in-the-loop.
architectural_implications.before: Humans read eval dashboards and edit prompts/configs manually.
architectural_implications.consequence: New safety surface: config-rewriting agents need their own eval and rollback, since their output changes production behavior broadly.
architectural_implications.observation: An agent (the diagnoser) now sits in the tuning/configuration layer, not only in the inference path.

architectural_implications.after: Separate loops per signal scope, with the marketplace loop sliced by geography, device type, and dish type.
architectural_implications.before: One offline eval suite used as the proxy for all quality questions.
architectural_implications.consequence: Teams must reconcile conflicting signals across loops and decide which layer owns a given regression.
architectural_implications.observation: Evaluation is stratified into three loops with distinct signal types (human labels, internal feedback, business A/B metrics).

article_ideas.angle: Invert the standard build order using a single production case: show which tuning capabilities became possible only because the logging contract existed up front, and what breaks when the schema drifts.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform and observability engineers building multi-agent production systems
article_ideas.based_on: the logging schema is effectively the interface
article_ideas.thesis: Teams that build agents and then bolt on observability cannot build self-learning loops; the flat per-step record contract must be designed first because it is the substrate that every tuning loop consumes, and it therefore deserves versioning discipline like any other public interface.
article_ideas.title: Your Trace Schema Is the Real Agent Interface

article_ideas.angle: Walk through the recall-first routing decision and show how the accepted precision loss (routing high-quality images needlessly) is a compute line item, not a quality bug.
article_ideas.audience: ML engineers owning cost-sensitive inference pipelines
article_ideas.based_on: choose the guardrail metric by the asymmetry of downstream cost
article_ideas.thesis: Choosing recall for a gating classifier is not a generic best practice but a statement about asymmetric downstream cost; teams should derive the guardrail metric from the price of each error and evaluate the router on a cost-weighted confusion matrix instead of F1.
article_ideas.title: Recall Is a Budget Decision, Not a Quality Preference

article_ideas.angle: Reframe the sample, compare, diagnose, rewrite, redeploy loop as a code-generation pipeline and apply the same release engineering rigor to it.

article_ideas.thesis: Moving drift remediation from a human reading dashboards to a diagnoser agent that rewrites configuration relocates responsibility for correctness: the config becomes generated output, so it needs its own canary, shadow evaluation, and rollback path before any loop closes automatically.
article_ideas.title: Putting an LLM in the Tuning Layer Changes Who Owns Drift

article_ideas.angle: Use the uniform-prompt collapse as the concrete illustration of a metric that is invisible to item-level evaluation but decisive for marketplace trust.

connections.relationship: The tuning loop consumes per-step JSON traces as its input substrate, making logging a hard dependency rather than a parallel concern.
Drift remediation is implemented as automated config rewriting, turning prompt/config artifacts into machine-editable outputs.
A recall-first router intentionally over-routes items into the expensive generation stage, trading compute for quality.
Comparing outputs against their own inputs gives a regression check that a scalar quality model cannot provide.
Business-level A/B results and human-labeled offline evals are two layers of the same eval stack and must be reconciled when they disagree.

evidence_quotes.text: End-to-end logging is critical to set up first before building self-learning loops.
All agent steps are logged in a flat JSON structure using Arize for observability and debugging.
Without comprehensive, flat JSON logging across all agent steps from the start, it is impossible to optimize or build self-learning loops.

core_insights.generalization: For any multi-agent pipeline intended to be auto-tuned, define the per-step record contract before the agent behavior, not after.
core_insights.insight: Establish end-to-end structured logging (flat JSON per agent step, via Arize) as a prerequisite to any self-learning loop; the logging schema is effectively the interface that makes closed-loop tuning possible at all.
core_insights.why_it_matters: It inverts the usual build order: teams typically build agents, then bolt on observability. Here telemetry is the foundation that later eval/tuning loops consume, so retrofitting it is expensive.

evidence_quotes.text: Routing guardrail metric is recall to prevent bad images from slipping into the system.
Routing failure precision miss: high-quality cheeseburger image incorrectly flagged as low quality.

core_insights.generalization: In gated pipelines, choose the guardrail metric by the asymmetry of downstream cost, not by generic F1-style balance.
core_insights.insight: The routing guardrail metric is deliberately asymmetric: recall is the optimization target so bad images cannot slip into the system, accepting over-enhancement (precision loss) as the cheaper error.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Picking recall over precision is a value judgment encoded as a metric, and it directly determines which failure examples the team treats as bugs.

evidence_quotes.text: Online tuning pipeline samples production data regularly, compares against human labels, and triggers auto-tuning via a diagnoser agent.
Using a diagnoser agent to analyze production drift, rewrite agent configurations, and trigger auto-tuning pipelines keeps systems sharp over time.

core_insights.generalization: Closed-loop self-tuning can be structured as: sample -> label-compare -> diagnose -> rewrite config -> redeploy, with an agent owning the diagnose/rewrite step.
core_insights.insight: A diagnoser agent closes the loop by sampling production data, comparing against human labels, rewriting agent configurations, and triggering auto-tuning pipelines — shifting human effort from labeling decisions to authoring guidelines and letting config rewrite be automated.
core_insights.why_it_matters: This puts an LLM inside the tuning layer of the system, not just the inference layer, which changes where drift remediation responsibility lives.

evidence_quotes.text: Model loop addresses drift against offline human labels.
Dogfooding loop collects internal thumbs up/down and freeform feedback from merchants and designers.
Marketplace loop measures business metrics like conversion rate via A/B experimentation.
Slicing marketplace conversion data by geography, device type, and dish type to tune specific segments.

core_insights.generalization: Design eval as a hierarchy from model-level regression signals up to end-business outcome metrics, and slice the top layer by segment to localize tuning.
core_insights.insight: Three nested feedback loops operate at different signal scopes — model loop (drift vs offline human labels), dogfooding loop (internal thumbs up/down and freeform merchant/designer feedback), marketplace loop (business conversion via A/B testing) — with per-segment slicing by geography, device type, and dish type.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Treating eval as a layered stack with distinct signal sources and scopes prevents conflating model-quality drift with business-metric drift, which require different remediation.

evidence_quotes.text: QA gate checks faithfulness, portion size, natural plating, colors/textures, and sharpness.
Pairwise comparison (pass@k) assesses whether the generated image is a better version of the original.
Failure example: added shrimp to crab legs, failing faithfulness.

core_insights.generalization: For enhancement/edit agents, evaluate each output against its own input as a pairwise baseline, not only against an absolute quality rubric.
core_insights.insight: Generation quality is enforced by a composition of a multi-dimension QA gate (faithfulness, portion size, natural plating, colors/textures, sharpness) plus pairwise pass@k comparison against the original, rather than a single scalar score.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Pairwise-vs-original framing directly targets regressions (edits that are worse than the input), which absolute quality scores cannot detect; the multi-dimension gate separately catches specific hallucination classes like added ingredients.

evidence_quotes.text: Must stay faithful to original image, preserve merchant brand identity, and avoid sameness across marketplace images.
Having the same prompt for every photo would collapse marketplace diversity.

core_insights.generalization: When an agent acts on many items in a shared surface, add cross-item distributional constraints to the objective, not just per-item quality gates.
core_insights.insight: Agent goals are encoded as a constrained triple — stay faithful, preserve brand, avoid sameness — making diversity across the marketplace an explicit objective rather than a byproduct; a uniform prompt would collapse it.
core_insights.why_it_matters: Introces a global, cross-item metric (sameness) that a per-item eval harness cannot measure, forcing a marketplace-level view into the eval design.

evidence_quotes.text: Routing agent decides whether to enhance or skip based on rubrics (technical, composition, content, policy, dish match).
Routing agent evaluates technical quality; if below par, sends to image editing agent.

core_insights.generalization: Where a generative step is expensive, the classifier in front of it should be evaluated on the cost-weighted confusion matrix, not accuracy.
core_insights.insight: Routing is rubric-based and selective (technical, composition, content, policy, dish match), so most items can skip the expensive generative path — evaluation of the router therefore has direct cost implications for the whole pipeline.
core_insights.why_it_matters: The router is both a quality gate and a cost-control valve; its recall target means it must bias toward routing more items into generation.

evidence_quotes.text: Online tuning pipeline samples production data regularly, compares against human labels, and triggers auto-tuning via a diagnoser agent.
Using a diagnoser agent to analyze production drift, rewrite agent configurations, and trigger auto-tuning pipelines keeps systems sharp over time.

deep_dives.topic: Guardrails for agents that rewrite production configuration
deep_dives.trigger_insight: What guardrails constrain the diagnoser agent when it rewrites configurations
deep_dives.why: The talk places an LLM in the tuning layer, not just the inference layer. That creates a new class of production change whose blast radius spans every routed item, yet no promotion gate is described. Without a promotion contract, drift remediation and drift causation become indistinguishable.

evidence_quotes.text: Must stay faithful to original image, preserve merchant brand identity, and avoid sameness across marketplace images.
Having the same prompt for every photo would collapse marketplace diversity.

deep_dives.research_question: Which distributional diversity metrics over generated image sets (embedding spread, prompt/style entropy, pairwise perceptual distance) correlate with marketplace conversion, and can a per-item eval harness detect a collapse toward sameness?
deep_dives.topic: Quantifying 'avoid sameness' as a marketplace-level eval metric
deep_dives.why: The objective triple explicitly includes a cross-item constraint that no per-item quality gate can observe. If sameness is not measured, a locally improving agent can monotonically degrade the shared marketplace surface while every item-level metric stays green.

evidence_quotes.text: Slicing marketplace conversion data by geography, device type, and dish type to tune specific segments.
Model loop addresses drift against offline human labels.

deep_dives.research_question: How should production samples be stratified (by geography, device type, dish type, merchant tier) so that label-distribution drift is detected before it moves marketplace metrics, and what sampling cadence bounds detection latency?
deep_dives.topic: Representativeness and staleness control in production sampling for drift detection
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How does the pipeline guarantee that production samples used for drift detection remain representative
deep_dives.why: The entire closed loop is only as good as the sample it diagnoses. If sampling is unstratified or silently stale, the diagnoser rewrites configs in response to a distribution that no longer exists, and auto-tuning becomes a drift amplifier rather than a corrector.

evidence_quotes.text: Routing guardrail metric is recall to prevent bad images from slipping into the system.
Routing failure precision miss: high-quality cheeseburger image incorrectly flagged as low quality.
Routing agent decides whether to enhance or skip based on rubrics (technical, composition, content, policy, dish match).

deep_dives.research_question: Does optimizing the router's recall-first guardrail on a cost-weighted confusion matrix rather than on F1 change the routing threshold enough to materially alter generation spend per thousand items at constant quality?
deep_dives.topic: Cost-weighted evaluation of the router as a compute valve
deep_dives.trigger_insight: evaluated on the cost-weighted confusion matrix
deep_dives.why: The router is simultaneously the quality gate and the spend control for the whole pipeline, so its threshold is an economic parameter. A precision miss documented in the talk (a good cheeseburger flagged as low quality) is not a quality bug but a budget line item, and should be evaluated as one.

evidence_quotes.text: Pairwise comparison (pass@k) assesses whether the generated image is a better version of the original.
Human labelers serve as the golden source of truth to remove subjective biases.
QA gate checks faithfulness, portion size, natural plating, colors/textures, and sharpness.

deep_dives.research_question: How much do automated pairwise-vs-original pass@k judgments agree with human pairwise labels, and does agreement hold across dish types where portion size and plating expectations differ?
deep_dives.topic: Calibrating pairwise pass@k against human pairwise judgment
deep_dives.trigger_insight: How much do pairwise pass@k scores agree with the human-labeled golden source
deep_dives.why: The QA stack combines a multi-dimension rubric, pairwise comparison, and human labels, but if pass@k diverges from human judgment per segment it will silently validate edits that the golden source rejects, making the two layers of the eval stack contradictory rather than layered.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Soumya Gupta, Jai Chopra
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Building closed-loop evaluations for multimodal agents at Uber scale
  • Purpose: To share production-grade engineering practices for building, evaluating, and self-tuning multimodal AI agents at scale using closed-loop eval pipelines. Soumya Gupta and Jai Chopra from Uber explain how they designed real-world production evaluations and closed-loop feedback systems for multimodal agents handling food photography enhancement on Uber Eats. They cover agent architecture (image understanding, routing, generation, QA), offline human alignment, routing and generation evaluations, failure modes, and three feedback loops (model loop, dogfooding loop, marketplace loop) to maintain high agent performance at scale.

Topic Map

Introduction & Uber Eats Scale

  • Explanation: Introduction of the speakers from Uber computer vision team and context on Uber Eats scale ($90B run rate, millions of items added monthly, 20% YoY growth, 10,000+ cities globally).
  • Key claims:
    • Uber Eats delivery marketplace is just as big as the mobility side.
    • Visual content plays a critical role in user experience and initial impressions.
    • Smaller, independent merchants lack time, know-how, and budget for professional food photography.
  • Examples:
    • Merchants updating menus frequently face high costs for professional photo shoots.
  • Terminology:
    • Uber Eats
    • multimodal agent
    • food photography
  • Why it matters: Establishes the massive business scale and real-world stakes of automated image enhancement.

Agent Goals & Spectrum of Agency

  • Explanation: Defining the core goals for the image-editing agent (stay faithful, preserve brand, avoid sameness) and balancing determinism versus creativity on the agency spectrum.
  • Key claims:
    • Consumers want authentic photos and actively distrust AI-generated food photography.
    • Must stay faithful to original image, preserve merchant brand identity, and avoid sameness across marketplace images.
    • Agents provide the right balance between deterministic rules and high agency creativity.
  • Examples:
    • Having the same prompt for every photo would collapse marketplace diversity.
  • Terminology:
    • stay faithful
    • preserve brand
    • avoid sameness
    • agency spectrum
  • Why it matters: Sets the design constraints and guiding principles required for consumer trust in a marketplace.

Agent Orchestration & Logging

  • Explanation: Detailed walkthrough of the end-to-end orchestration pipeline: image quality understanding, routing, prompting, generation, LLM QA, post-processing, and logging.
  • Key claims:
    • End-to-end logging is critical to set up first before building self-learning loops.
    • All agent steps are logged in a flat JSON structure using Arize for observability and debugging.
    • Routing agent decides whether to enhance or skip based on rubrics (technical, composition, content, policy, dish match).
  • Examples:
    • Routing agent evaluates technical quality; if below par, sends to image editing agent.
  • Terminology:
    • orchestration
    • routing agent
    • LLM QA
    • Arize
    • logging
  • Why it matters: Provides a reproducible, observable architecture for multi-agent workflows in production.

Routing Evals: Offline Human Alignment

  • Explanation: How to evaluate and align the routing agent using human labels, precision/recall metrics, and handling drift online.
  • Key claims:
    • Human labelers serve as the golden source of truth to remove subjective biases.
    • Routing guardrail metric is recall to prevent bad images from slipping into the system.
    • Online tuning pipeline samples production data regularly, compares against human labels, and triggers auto-tuning via a diagnoser agent.
  • Examples:
    • Routing failure precision miss: high-quality cheeseburger image incorrectly flagged as low quality.
  • Terminology:
    • human alignment
    • recall
    • precision
    • confusion matrix
    • diagnoser agent
  • Why it matters: Ensures that automated routing aligns with human standards without requiring manual intervention at scale.

Generation Evals & Pairwise Comparison

  • Explanation: Evaluating image generation and enhancement using prompt generation, multi-dimensional QA gates, pass@k metrics, and pairwise comparisons.
  • Key claims:
    • Generation pipeline uses a 3-step process: generate prompt, enhance image, and pass through QA gate.
    • QA gate checks faithfulness, portion size, natural plating, colors/textures, and sharpness.
    • Pairwise comparison (pass@k) assesses whether the generated image is a better version of the original.
  • Examples:
    • Failure example: added shrimp to crab legs, failing faithfulness.
  • Terminology:
    • QA gate
    • pass@k
    • pairwise comparison
    • reward hacking
  • Why it matters: Prevents hallucinated food items, reward hacking, and unrealistic edits from reaching production menus.

Closed-Loop Feedback Systems

  • Explanation: Overview of the three feedback loops: Model Loop, Dogfooding Loop, and Marketplace Loop.
  • Key claims:
    • Model loop addresses drift against offline human labels.
    • Dogfooding loop collects internal thumbs up/down and freeform feedback from merchants and designers.
    • Marketplace loop measures business metrics like conversion rate via A/B experimentation.
  • Examples:
    • Slicing marketplace conversion data by geography, device type, and dish type to tune specific segments.
  • Terminology:
    • model loop
    • dogfooding loop
    • marketplace loop
    • diagnoser
    • conversion rate
  • Why it matters: Enables continuous self-improvement and marketplace optimization without human-in-the-loop bottlenecks.

Key Points

End-to-end logging must be established first

  • Explanation: Without comprehensive, flat JSON logging across all agent steps from the start, it is impossible to optimize or build self-learning loops.
  • Evidence: Mentioned during agent orchestration discussion and code overview using Arize.
  • Practical implication: Engineers should prioritize telemetry and structured logging before building complex agent feedback mechanisms.

Human labels as the golden source of truth

  • Explanation: Using objective guidelines for human labelers removes subjective bias and provides a reliable baseline for offline alignment.
  • Evidence: Offline human alignment workflow for routing and generation evals.
  • Practical implication: Invest in clean, unbiased human-labeled evaluation datasets before training or tuning agent prompts.

Config-driven automated tuning pipelines

  • Explanation: Using a diagnoser agent to analyze production drift, rewrite agent configurations, and trigger auto-tuning pipelines keeps systems sharp over time.
  • Evidence: Detailed explanation of online tuning focused on drift without human-in-the-loop.
  • Practical implication: Automate closed-loop tuning to reduce maintenance overhead for production AI agents.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Multimodal Agent Orchestration Pipeline

  • How it works: Inputs pass through image quality understanding, routing, prompting, generation, LLM QA, and post-processing gates.
  • Components:
    • Image Quality Understanding
    • Routing Agent
    • Prompting Agent
    • Generation / Editing Agent
    • LLM QA Gate
    • Publish Ready QA
  • When to use: When building production multimodal AI workflows requiring strict quality, safety, and brand alignment.

Closed-Loop Feedback Framework

  • How it works: Combines production data, human labels, and feedback loops into a diagnoser agent that auto-tunes agent configurations and benchmarks them against gold standards.
  • Components:
    • Diagnoser Agent
    • Reflect Sub-agent
    • Synthesize Sub-agent
    • Agent Config Store
    • Evaluator & Benchmark Engine
  • When to use: When maintaining agent performance against model drift and data changes in production.

Examples & Case Studies

An image of 6 chicken wings passed routing with a dish name of 8 pieces chicken wings.

  • Illustrates: Recall miss in routing where the agent approved an incorrect count.
  • Lesson: Static offline models fail on edge cases; prompt and system alignment must evolve continuously.

An image enhancement agent added shrimp to a crab leg dish and removed sauce from sushi.

  • Illustrates: Faithfulness and completeness failure modes in generation.
  • Lesson: Rigorous QA gates and pairwise comparison evals are needed to catch hallucinations and reward hacking.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Implement structured end-to-end logging before building agent optimization loops.
    • Define clear rubric-based evaluation criteria (technical, composition, policy, dish match).
  • Strategic:
    • Balance agent agency and determinism to maintain safety without sacrificing creativity.
    • Build config-driven automated tuning pipelines to combat production data drift.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How to scale human labeling cost-effectively for high-throughput multimodal applications?
    • What are the best automated metrics to detect subtle reward hacking in image generation?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • Uber Eats delivery marketplace is comparable in scale to the mobility side. (business scale)
  • End-to-end logging in a flat JSON structure significantly simplifies root-cause diagnosis for non-technical team members. (engineering practice)

Notable Quotes

"Building Closed-Loop Evals for a Multimodal Agent at Uber Scale" "End to end logging is important to setup first" (at 10:23)

Compressed Summary

  • Uber Eats scales food photography enhancement using multimodal agents.
  • Key goals: stay faithful, preserve brand, avoid sameness.
  • Architecture includes image understanding, routing, generation, LLM QA, and publishing gates.
  • Three feedback loops: model loop, dogfooding loop, and marketplace loop.
  • Diagnoser agent automates config tuning using production feedback without human intervention.
  • Keywords: multimodal agent, evaluations, closed-loop, image enhancement, uber scale

- **Main topic**: Building closed-loop evaluations for multimodal agents at Uber scale
- **Purpose**: To share production-grade engineering practices for building, evaluating, and self-tuning multimodal AI agents at scale using closed-loop eval pipelines.
Soumya Gupta and Jai Chopra from Uber explain how they designed real-world production evaluations and closed-loop feedback systems for multimodal agents handling food photography enhancement on Uber Eats. They cover agent architecture (image understanding, routing, generation, QA), offline human alignment, routing and generation evaluations, failure modes, and three feedback loops (model loop, dogfooding loop, marketplace loop) to maintain high agent performance at scale.
## Topic Map
### Introduction & Uber Eats Scale
- **Explanation**: Introduction of the speakers from Uber computer vision team and context on Uber Eats scale ($90B run rate, millions of items added monthly, 20% YoY growth, 10,000+ cities globally).
- **Key claims**:
  - Uber Eats delivery marketplace is just as big as the mobility side.
  - Visual content plays a critical role in user experience and initial impressions.
  - Smaller, independent merchants lack time, know-how, and budget for professional food photography.
- **Examples**:
  - Merchants updating menus frequently face high costs for professional photo shoots.
- **Terminology**:
  - Uber Eats
  - multimodal agent
  - food photography
- **Why it matters**: Establishes the massive business scale and real-world stakes of automated image enhancement.
### Agent Goals & Spectrum of Agency
- **Explanation**: Defining the core goals for the image-editing agent (stay faithful, preserve brand, avoid sameness) and balancing determinism versus creativity on the agency spectrum.
- **Key claims**:
  - Consumers want authentic photos and actively distrust AI-generated food photography.
  - Must stay faithful to original image, preserve merchant brand identity, and avoid sameness across marketplace images.
  - Agents provide the right balance between deterministic rules and high agency creativity.
- **Examples**:
  - Having the same prompt for every photo would collapse marketplace diversity.
- **Terminology**:
  - stay faithful
  - preserve brand
  - avoid sameness
  - agency spectrum
- **Why it matters**: Sets the design constraints and guiding principles required for consumer trust in a marketplace.
### Agent Orchestration & Logging
- **Explanation**: Detailed walkthrough of the end-to-end orchestration pipeline: image quality understanding, routing, prompting, generation, LLM QA, post-processing, and logging.
- **Key claims**:
  - End-to-end logging is critical to set up first before building self-learning loops.
  - All agent steps are logged in a flat JSON structure using Arize for observability and debugging.
  - Routing agent decides whether to enhance or skip based on rubrics (technical, composition, content, policy, dish match).
- **Examples**:
  - Routing agent evaluates technical quality; if below par, sends to image editing agent.
- **Terminology**:
  - orchestration
  - routing agent
  - LLM QA
  - Arize
  - logging
- **Why it matters**: Provides a reproducible, observable architecture for multi-agent workflows in production.
### Routing Evals: Offline Human Alignment
- **Explanation**: How to evaluate and align the routing agent using human labels, precision/recall metrics, and handling drift online.
- **Key claims**:
  - Human labelers serve as the golden source of truth to remove subjective biases.
  - Routing guardrail metric is recall to prevent bad images from slipping into the system.
  - Online tuning pipeline samples production data regularly, compares against human labels, and triggers auto-tuning via a diagnoser agent.
- **Examples**:
  - Routing failure precision miss: high-quality cheeseburger image incorrectly flagged as low quality.
- **Terminology**:
  - human alignment
  - recall
  - precision
  - confusion matrix
  - diagnoser agent
- **Why it matters**: Ensures that automated routing aligns with human standards without requiring manual intervention at scale.
### Generation Evals & Pairwise Comparison
- **Explanation**: Evaluating image generation and enhancement using prompt generation, multi-dimensional QA gates, pass@k metrics, and pairwise comparisons.
- **Key claims**:
  - Generation pipeline uses a 3-step process: generate prompt, enhance image, and pass through QA gate.
  - QA gate checks faithfulness, portion size, natural plating, colors/textures, and sharpness.
  - Pairwise comparison (pass@k) assesses whether the generated image is a better version of the original.
- **Examples**:
  - Failure example: added shrimp to crab legs, failing faithfulness.
- **Terminology**:
  - QA gate
  - pass@k
  - pairwise comparison
  - reward hacking
- **Why it matters**: Prevents hallucinated food items, reward hacking, and unrealistic edits from reaching production menus.
### Closed-Loop Feedback Systems
- **Explanation**: Overview of the three feedback loops: Model Loop, Dogfooding Loop, and Marketplace Loop.
- **Key claims**:
  - Model loop addresses drift against offline human labels.
  - Dogfooding loop collects internal thumbs up/down and freeform feedback from merchants and designers.
  - Marketplace loop measures business metrics like conversion rate via A/B experimentation.
- **Examples**:
  - Slicing marketplace conversion data by geography, device type, and dish type to tune specific segments.
- **Terminology**:
  - model loop
  - dogfooding loop
  - marketplace loop
  - diagnoser
  - conversion rate
- **Why it matters**: Enables continuous self-improvement and marketplace optimization without human-in-the-loop bottlenecks.
## Key Points
### End-to-end logging must be established first
- **Explanation**: Without comprehensive, flat JSON logging across all agent steps from the start, it is impossible to optimize or build self-learning loops.
- **Evidence**: Mentioned during agent orchestration discussion and code overview using Arize.
- **Practical implication**: Engineers should prioritize telemetry and structured logging before building complex agent feedback mechanisms.
### Human labels as the golden source of truth
- **Explanation**: Using objective guidelines for human labelers removes subjective bias and provides a reliable baseline for offline alignment.
- **Evidence**: Offline human alignment workflow for routing and generation evals.
- **Practical implication**: Invest in clean, unbiased human-labeled evaluation datasets before training or tuning agent prompts.
### Config-driven automated tuning pipelines
- **Explanation**: Using a diagnoser agent to analyze production drift, rewrite agent configurations, and trigger auto-tuning pipelines keeps systems sharp over time.
- **Evidence**: Detailed explanation of online tuning focused on drift without human-in-the-loop.
- **Practical implication**: Automate closed-loop tuning to reduce maintenance overhead for production AI agents.
## Frameworks, Models & Processes
### Multimodal Agent Orchestration Pipeline
- **How it works**: Inputs pass through image quality understanding, routing, prompting, generation, LLM QA, and post-processing gates.
- **Components**:
  - Image Quality Understanding
  - Routing Agent
  - Prompting Agent
  - Generation / Editing Agent
  - LLM QA Gate
  - Publish Ready QA
- **When to use**: When building production multimodal AI workflows requiring strict quality, safety, and brand alignment.
### Closed-Loop Feedback Framework
- **How it works**: Combines production data, human labels, and feedback loops into a diagnoser agent that auto-tunes agent configurations and benchmarks them against gold standards.
- **Components**:
  - Diagnoser Agent
  - Reflect Sub-agent
  - Synthesize Sub-agent
  - Agent Config Store
  - Evaluator & Benchmark Engine
- **When to use**: When maintaining agent performance against model drift and data changes in production.
## Examples & Case Studies
### An image of 6 chicken wings passed routing with a dish name of 8 pieces chicken wings.
- **Illustrates**: Recall miss in routing where the agent approved an incorrect count.
- **Lesson**: Static offline models fail on edge cases; prompt and system alignment must evolve continuously.
### An image enhancement agent added shrimp to a crab leg dish and removed sauce from sushi.
- **Illustrates**: Faithfulness and completeness failure modes in generation.
- **Lesson**: Rigorous QA gates and pairwise comparison evals are needed to catch hallucinations and reward hacking.
## Actionable Takeaways
- **Immediate**:
  - Implement structured end-to-end logging before building agent optimization loops.
  - Define clear rubric-based evaluation criteria (technical, composition, policy, dish match).
- **Strategic**:
  - Balance agent agency and determinism to maintain safety without sacrificing creativity.
  - Build config-driven automated tuning pipelines to combat production data drift.
- **Questions to investigate**:
  - How to scale human labeling cost-effectively for high-throughput multimodal applications?
  - What are the best automated metrics to detect subtle reward hacking in image generation?
## Claims Worth Verifying
- Uber Eats delivery marketplace is comparable in scale to the mobility side. (business scale)
- End-to-end logging in a flat JSON structure significantly simplifies root-cause diagnosis for non-technical team members. (engineering practice)

- Key goals: stay faithful, preserve brand, avoid sameness.
- Architecture includes image understanding, routing, generation, LLM QA, and publishing gates.
- Three feedback loops: model loop, dogfooding loop, and marketplace loop.
- Diagnoser agent automates config tuning using production feedback without human intervention.
